doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Coming to Los Angeles and the studio orchestras
summary: His first trips west with Les, and the contracted studio orchestras at Fox, MGM and others.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well you got out here, and gee, things have changed dramatically.
Boy. You’re talking about now, what time period are you talking about?
You’re talking about, you came out here in ’49 or—

Oh the very first time with Les was ’38. I mean just before I did those recordings with him back east, this was one of the stops we made. I guess we played the Palladium, stuff like that. So that was the earliest. Then we came out the second time, that was also a Palladium stop and that’s when they asked us to join Fox Studios. But quite a change, yes. And there were studio orchestras which I was now part of. The Twentieth Century Fox band, which was a complete orchestra, like 50 or 60 or 70 or even more people, and each independent studio — I don’t mean independent, MGM had it’s own orchestra, Twentieth Century Fox, Universal, Warner Brothers, you name it. Every— Columbia.

Each studio had its own orchestra and they were all great. And each orchestra was under contract, and everybody in the orchestra had a weekly salary. It was the best of all worlds at that time, and I fortunately fell into it after I had been with Les Brown for a while. So I lucked out. I was in the right place at the right time.
